headline: Majors hold above 200-day lines with momentum rolling over, while whales accumulate onto exchanges and ETH ETF absorbs inflows against Bitcoin outflows.
paragraphs: The regime is firm: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day moving averages, and four of the five carry golden crosses (XRP alone lacks one). The 200-day trend is unified across the constellation. That structural floor, however, sits atop a momentum picture that is rolling over quietly. Every major asset, from Bitcoin through Solana and BNB, shows MACD below its signal line. RSI across the group (Bitcoin 59.3, Ethereum 61.7, Solana 57.4, XRP 58.0, BNB 57.1) runs in the mid-50s to low-60s: neutral to mildly elevated, but not extended. This is a trend that has legs to stand on, but the accelerant has burned off. Bitcoin up 2.4% on the day masks a weekly decline of 1.2% and sits 36.9% below its 12-month high; the monthly climb of 23.89% is real, yet the tape refuses to confirm upside breakout momentum.

Leverage positioning shows funding rates still positive but cooling. Bitcoin's 8-hour funding at 0.52% (annualized to 5.7%) and Ethereum's at 0.32% (3.5% annualized) represent bulls paying to hold, but neither rate is steep. Bitcoin's long-to-short ratio stands at 1.29, Ethereum at 1.38; positioned, but not dangerously so. The outliers are SOL, XRP, and DOGE: Solana's 10.9% annualized funding and XRP's 11.0% show genuine crowding in longs, with long-to-short ratios of 1.95 and 2.29 respectively. DOGE is most extreme at 4.32 long-to-short, though its open interest (under $87 million) is small relative to the flagship assets. Liquidations over the most recent window show shorts being flushed from Bitcoin (852k over one hour, zero longs) and Ethereum (1M shorts, zero longs), a tell that recent rallies have caught short-side overextension. Solana's liquidations over four hours split both ways (698k longs, 246k shorts), signaling two-way churn.

Whale flows paint a story of accumulation onto venues over the 72-hour window: $226.8 million net Bitcoin moving onto exchanges, with Coinbase receiving 164.8 million USD worth on the inflow side and losing 77.3 and 57.5 million on the outflow leg. Stablecoin movements support the picture, with 170.8 million USDC onto Kraken and 157.1 million USDT onto Binance over the same period. The weekly trend, however, reverses sharply: week ending Sep 07 saw $267 million net moving OFF exchanges, but week ending Sep 14 flipped to $725 million moving ONTO exchanges. This is not a quiet flow; the inflection is sharp. Stablecoin float at 310 billion USD has grown 1.24% over the month, modest fuel for a 2.69 trillion dollar market cap.

ETF flows present a clean split. Bitcoin spot ETF saw outflows of 13.2 million USD on Sep 11 and a net outflow of 288.1 million over the last five sessions, with four days of same-direction selling. Ethereum ETF received 216.4 million USD on Sep 11 and a net inflow of 222.8 million over five sessions, with only one day of agreement but the direction constant. The divergence is the read: traditional finance is rotating out of Bitcoin and into Ethereum. Bitcoin still dominates spot at 58.6% of total market cap, and total cap declined 0.2% on the day despite intra-day rallies across most names.

Sentiment sits at 57 (greed), within a 30-day range of 31 to 74, squarely middling. The crowd is neither panicked nor euphoric, which tracks the tape: no fresh breakout momentum, no capitulation, a consolidation at support with old-money liquidations clearing the way. The outliers merit watching. DOGE is below its 200-day line with an RSI of 51.1 (neutral-bearish) and is down 0.56% on the week despite being up 2.28% on the day, a chop that speaks to confusion. ADA sits below trend at 0.2107 USD with an RSI of 53.3, up 3.49% on the day but down 0.22% on the week and trailing the month's 11.29% gain. These are laggards wearing the coat of a rally.

The window to watch: Can Bitcoin reclaim weekly positive territory while MACD signals remain below line, or does the week-long drift extend and carve the real trend lower? Bitcoin's recent high within the range was 81,264.70; a push back above that on fresh momentum would challenge the divergence. Ethereum's sustained ETF inflows against Bitcoin's outflows, paired with maintained position above 200-day, would mark a tactical shift in institutional appetite. Finally, the 200-day lines themselves remain the floor; a break below, especially one that breaks the golden cross, would be the regime change worth naming.
